title: Boolean Functions
question: What exactly is to be computed, independent of how?

title: What does a bit string mean?
takeaway: Meaning comes from the encoding. Cost is measured by input length: \(N\) needs about \(\log_2N\) bits.

title: What does a yes/no question compute?
takeaway: A truth table says what the answer is, not how to get it, and an \(n\)-bit function has \(2^n\) rows.

title: Can a truth table become a formula?
steps: Work modulo two: \(1+1=0\), so \(+\) is XOR and \(\times\) is AND.
A row detector, \(\delta_s(x)=\prod_{s_i=1}x_i\prod_{s_i=0}(1+x_i)\), equals 1 only on row \(s\).
Add the detectors of the rows where \(f=1\).
takeaway: Every Boolean function is a polynomial in its input bits.

title: Boolean Circuits
question: How does a formula become a sequence of operations?

title: One gate at a time
lead: Evaluate \(x+y+xy\): AND for the product, XOR for the sums.
takeaway: Every Boolean function has a circuit. Not necessarily a small one.

title: Do we need more than one kind of gate?
lead: \(\operatorname{NAND}(a,a)=\neg a\); NOT of NAND is AND; four NANDs make XOR.
takeaway: NAND is universal. Classically, copying a bit to several gates (fan-out) is free.

title: Can we undo AND?
question: An AND gate outputs 0. Which input produced it?
answer: Any of 00, 01, or 10. AND merges inputs, so it has no inverse.
notes: Always say which registers are kept: a circuit can discard a copy and still keep enough elsewhere to recover its input.

title: Information Erasure
question: Does losing information have a physical price?

title: What does erasing a bit cost?
label: Landauer’s principle (quoted result)
statement: Erasing one equally likely bit, without keeping its value elsewhere, releases at least \(k_{\mathrm B}T\ln2\) of heat on average.
note: A bit already known to be 0 can be left alone. A biased bit, or one with a record elsewhere, costs less, but the record must be counted too.

title: Is reversible the same as cool?

left.label: Logically reversible
items: Avoids the cost that erasure forces.
A real device may still dissipate energy.

right.label: Run slowly
items: AND run slowly still merges inputs.
Reversibility is a property of the map, not its speed.

takeaway: Keep apart two questions: can the map be inverted, and how much energy does the device use?

title: Can every function be computed without erasure?
steps: Apply twice: \(t\oplus f(x)\oplus f(x)=t\). \(U_f\) is its own inverse.
\(f\) still merges inputs; the larger map does not.
takeaway: The extra bits are what make the transformation one-to-one.

title: Reversible Gates
question: Which gates carry out a reversible embedding?

title: How can one bit control another without loss?
steps: Keep the control; let it choose a reversible update of the target.
Applying it twice restores both bits: the control tells us what was done.
Discard the control and we cannot undo the flip.

title: Which reversible gates suffice?
takeaway: With the target 1, Toffoli gives NAND; CNOT copies a bit onto 0. So Toffoli gates build every circuit reversibly.
notes: Fredkin gates are also universal with suitable constants and workspace; we quote that result.

title: What do we do with leftover workspace?
lead: Compute, copy the answer, then run the computation backward.
takeaway: Only the input and the answer remain. In quantum computing, leftover records would block interference.

title: What we found
items: Encodings turn tasks into Boolean functions; every function is a polynomial over bits.
Circuits evaluate any function, and NAND alone is enough.
Erasing information has a minimum heat cost; merging inputs forces erasure.
Keeping the input makes every function reversible: Toffoli gates do it.
Uncomputation clears the workspace without erasing it.
